headline: Structural variants, polygenic axes and mtDNA regulation across genomic scales
label: Comparative Regulatory Genomics Evolution
summary: Rare-variant GWAS confounding and mtDNA expression decoupling are refining how genomic variation is linked to function and trait architecture.
synthesis: The items converge on how genomic variation shapes expression and trait architecture beyond simple gene-level models. A population-genomic study of four Atlantic salmon lineages tracks structural variant persistence and recurrent emergence using SV discovery, local PCA and haplotype-distance analysis. In human genetics, a gene-distal polygenic axis, extracted by SVD of signed regional medians across 403 GWAS, is the dominant axis of trait covariation yet sits below genome-wide significance. A UK Biobank analysis of 306,991 exomes shows that stratification and assortative mating drive rare-variant GWAS false positives, with family designs helping. Across 731 lymphoblastoid cell lines and GTEx tissues, mtDNA copy number is largely decoupled from mtDNA expression. Together these results argue that regulatory and distal architecture, along with careful confounder control, are central to interpreting genomic association and evolutionary signal.
